turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Well, I came in because... I just can't stop focusing on my face. Specifically, the left side of it. It looks really uneven and puffy to me. 

I notice it constantly, especially when I'm on video calls for work, or if I see photos of myself from my salsa dancing group. Everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything, but I know what I'm looking at. It's just... it's starting to really mess with my work and my social life, so I figured I needed to talk to someone about it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes a constant preoccupation with a perceived flaw in their face (uneven and puffy left side) that others say they cannot see.

turns.doctor_question: Because of how you feel about your face, do you find yourself spending time repeatedly checking mirrors, trying to hide it, or comparing your appearance to others?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I definitely do. Especially before my work meetings or if I'm getting ready to go out. I'll just... keep opening the camera preview on my computer or phone. I spend a lot of time changing the angle and messing with the lighting, just trying to see how bad it looks. 

And I'm constantly fixing my hair to kind of cover up that side of my face. If it's a photo, I end up retaking it over and over. I also ask my friends if I look strange, probably way more than I should. Honestly, by the time I'm done doing all of that, I'm usually either running late or I'm just... too drained to even go out anymore.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors such as repeatedly checking camera previews, adjusting lighting, covering their face with hair, and seeking reassurance from friends about their appearance.

turns.doctor_question: Deep down, do you ever think that your perception might be exaggerating things and that others are truly right, or are you completely convinced that your face looks uneven?
turns.patient_response:
I guess... I'm kind of torn on that. Logically, when everyone keeps telling me they don't see it, a part of me thinks maybe I am blowing it out of proportion. Like, they can't all be wrong, right? 

But then... I look at the camera preview or the mirror, and it's just so obvious to me. It really doesn't feel exaggerated when I'm looking right at it. So, I want to believe them, but it's just really hard to accept that they're right when my own eyes are telling me it's uneven.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes a perceived flaw (uneven face) that others tell them they do not see, which is the core feature of preoccupation with an unobservable or slight appearance defect.
